title: ReCite: Agentic Reasoning for Faithful Citation

numericClaims.quote: To support this task, we construct 31,118 samples (comprising 28,006 for training and 3,112 for testing)

We isolate 7,079 high-density paragraphs (comprising 6,779 for training and 300 for testing) whose BibTeX entries contain complete titles and abstracts, and use DeepSeek-V3 in a posterior setting: with full access to the target reference’s metadata, it retroactively deduces a logical reasoning path (<reasoning>) and an optimal keyword set (<keywords>) for each citation (Listing 1).
The 90.6% average accuracy (Cohen’s κ = 0.805) confirms the reliability of the synthesized data.
We construct 2,000 trajectories in total: 500 “gold” paths and 1,500 reflection-enhanced variants.
Specifically, we randomly sample 50 paragraphs from CVPR’25, EMNLP’24, ICCV’23, and NeurIPS’25, yielding 200 paragraphs in total.
An audit confirms that none of the 2,640 training citation decisions involved any of the 1,023 test papers.
For each query, GRPO samples a group of G = 4 candidate outputs and updates the policy with their relative advantages, eliminating the need for a separate value network.
For SFT, we use an 8-bit Paged AdamW optimizer (learning rate 2 × 10−5, 3 epochs, cosine decay, 5% warmup).

As shown in Table 3, ReCite-SFT(CAP-8) achieves the highest Strict F1 of 39.15%, outperforming every baseline including DeepSeek-V4-Pro and Qwen3.6-Plus, demonstrating the effectiveness of our decoupled agentic design.
QueryPlanner-SFT alone reaches Token F1 of 56.12%, approaching the 58.63% of DeepSeek-V3 (671B) and clearly beating the 27B open-source baseline.
Replacing CiteLocator causes a severe drop in Strict F1 to 2.75%, proving that logical breakpoint perception is the foundational prerequisite.

questions.question: What base model are all three ReCite modules built on?
questions.answer: Qwen3-4B — specifically Qwen3-4B-Instruct serves as the base model for all three modules, trained via SFT and (for QueryPlanner) GRPO.

questions.question: What are the three core modules of the ReCite framework and what does each do?
questions.answer: CiteLocator (citation location perception — predicts citation boundaries and Mandatory/Optional necessity labels), QueryPlanner (intent-aware query planning — generates a reasoning chain plus retrieval keywords per citation position), and Master Brain (task orchestration with reflective re-retrieval and verification).

questions.question: Into which two distinct forms does the paper decompose citation hallucinations, and which remains open?
questions.answer: Fabrication (inventing non-existent papers), largely resolved by retrieval-augmented architectures, and misattribution (citing authentic papers that fail to logically support the claim), which remains open and is ReCite's target.

questions.question: How large is the raw training corpus and where does it come from?
questions.answer: 10,893 LaTeX source packages crawled from arXiv, corresponding to papers published in 2024–2025 at top computer science venues including ACL, EMNLP, CVPR, ICCV, and NeurIPS.

questions.question: Which LLM was used to synthesize the supervision (necessity labels, posterior reasoning/keywords, and trajectory thinking)?
questions.answer: DeepSeek-V3 — used to annotate Mandatory/Optional necessity, to retroactively deduce reasoning paths and keyword sets in a posterior setting, and to deduce the <think> connecting observe/act pairs.

questions.question: At which three strictness levels are end-to-end workflows evaluated?
questions.answer: Overall-Strictly (exact target match: correct position AND exact ground-truth paper), Lenient Evaluation (accepts highly relevant substitute papers via LLM-as-a-Judge), and Position-Only (correct logical breakpoint regardless of retrieved candidate).

questions.question: What is ReCite-SFT(CAP-8)'s best Strict F1, and what Lenient F1 does it reach?
questions.answer: The highest Strict F1 of 39.15%, and a Lenient F1 of 55.14% — a 15.99% gain in Lenient F1 over ReCite-SFT.

questions.question: What number of retrieved candidate papers (Top-k) is chosen as optimal, and why?
questions.answer: k = 8: F1 improves up to k = 8 for both ReCite and the DeepSeek-V4-Flash baseline, after which improvements are limited by context noise, and larger k inflates input length and inference cost.

questions.question: Which external API does Master Brain query to fetch candidate metadata during inference?
questions.answer: The Semantic Scholar API, fetching title, abstract, authors, year, and citation count.

questions.question: What three components make up the composite GRPO reward for QueryPlanner?
questions.answer: Format compliance (penalizes deviations from the required <reasoning>/<keywords> layout), entity recall (against the target reference), and intent alignment (against the ground-truth intent).

questions.question: What hardware and systems were used to train and evaluate ReCite?
questions.answer: NVIDIA RTX 4090 D and A800 GPUs, with DeepSpeed for distributed training and vLLM (PagedAttention) for high-throughput inference.

questions.question: How was the end-to-end test set constructed and kept disjoint from training data?
questions.answer: 50 paragraphs were randomly sampled from each of CVPR’25, EMNLP’24, ICCV’23, and NeurIPS’25 (200 paragraphs total, 1,023 unique target test papers); an audit confirmed none of the 2,640 training citation decisions involved any of the 1,023 test papers.

questions.question: How many GPU-hours or dollars did it cost to train and run ReCite end-to-end?
How well does ReCite generalize to non-computer-science domains such as biomedical or humanities literature?
How many papers are indexed in the local retrieval database that the search_db_single tool queries?
